caption: What if you chased the hottest temperature ever? Start with India's hottest day on record: 51 °C in Phalodi, Rajasthan, on 19 May 2016. Go hotter and water boils at 100 °C, perfect for chai. Basalt lava erupts at up to about 1,200 °C. The Sun's surface is about 5,500 °C, yet a lightning bolt heats the air around it to roughly 30,000 °C, about five times hotter. Deep inside the Sun, the core sits near 15 million °C. Humans aim higher: fusion reactors like ITER, which India helps build, are designed to reach 150 million °C, ten times the Sun's core. The all-time record came in 2012, when CERN's Large Hadron Collider smashed lead ions into a quark-gluon soup of over 5 trillion degrees. Plot twist: the LHC's magnets are cooled to -271.3 °C, colder than outer space at -270.5 °C. Which number shocked YOU the most? 👇
